blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that the points whose position vectors are \(A(-6\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 2\underline{k})\), \(B(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 4\underline{k})\), \(C(5\underline{i} + 7\underline{j} + 3\underline{k})\), \(D(-13\underline{i} + 17\underline{j} - \underline{k})\) are coplanar.
blocks.explanation:
A coplanarity proof for four points.
We must show A, B, C, D lie in one plane.
Plan: make three vectors from one point, \(\overrightarrow{AB}, \overrightarrow{AC}, \overrightarrow{AD}\); the points are coplanar when these three vectors are, i.e. when their triple product is 0.
steps:
Given: the position vectors of \(A, B, C, D\).
To prove: \(A, B, C, D\) are coplanar.
Method: Four points lie in one plane exactly when \(\overrightarrow{AB}, \overrightarrow{AC}, \overrightarrow{AD}\) are coplanar, i.e. \([\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}] = 0\).

Find the three vectors from \(A\)
\[\overrightarrow{AB} = 9\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\]
\[\overrightarrow{AC} = 11\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + \underline{k}\]
\[\overrightarrow{AD} = -7\underline{i} + 14\underline{j} - 3\underline{k}\]
Why: \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) = (position vector of B) \(-\) (position vector of A), e.g. \(3 - (-6) = 9\), \(-2 - 3 = -5\), \(4 - 2 = 2\).

Conclude and check
\[\overrightarrow{AD} = -2\overrightarrow{AB} + \overrightarrow{AC}\]
\[-18 + 11 = -7,\ 10 + 4 = 14,\ -4 + 1 = -3 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The triple product is 0, so the three vectors, and hence the four points, are coplanar. The check shows \(\overrightarrow{AD}\) is built from \(\overrightarrow{AB}\) and \(\overrightarrow{AC}\).
blocks.final_answer: \([\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}] = 0\). Hence proved: \(A, B, C, D\) are coplanar.
